# The scanner .github/workflows/security.yml installs, pinned, in a file a bot can read.
#
# WHY THE VERSION IS NOT ON THE pip install LINE. A version written into a workflow step is
# watched by nothing at all: Dependabot reads manifests and `uses:` lines, and it does not read
# shell commands. A requirements file is an ecosystem it does read, so a new semgrep release
# arrives here as a pull request instead of ageing in silence. The full account of what that
# silence cost in another of this owner's repositories is in .github/dependabot.yml, above the
# pip entry that watches this file.
#
# WHY IT IS PINNED AT ALL. An analyser that updates itself changes the verdict of a merge gate
# without anybody changing the code, which is the one thing a merge gate must not do. A new
# release turning a green branch red on a commit that touched nothing teaches everybody to
# ignore the check.
#
# THE GATE'S NUMBERS ARE MEASURED WITH THE VERSION BELOW. Measured again on 2026-10-26, when the
# version moved from 1.180.0 to 1.181.0. The run is the Semgrep job of Dependabot's own pull request
# for that bump (run 40335089268, on the merge of its branch into main with `--config p/default`):
# the gate read zero blocking findings, zero scan errors, 680 files and 424 rules, and semgrep's own
# summary said it loaded 1074 code rules, ran 379 of them and found nothing. The two rule counts
# are one run read two ways - 379 is semgrep's own summary, 424 the timing list in the report,
# which is what the gate counts. For 1.180.0 on 2026-10-14 the same pair was 374 and 419, over 399
# files. Before that the numbers here were from 1.177.0 on 2026-09-22 (131 rules, 301 files), and
# 1.178.0 was never measured. Moving this line means measuring again rather than assuming the
# report will look the same.
#
# WHY 1.181.0 AND NOT THE NEWEST. 1.182.0 was uploaded on 2026-10-20 and 1.182.1 on 2026-10-22,
# both inside the seven days of cooldown .github/dependabot.yml asks for, and 1.181.0 (uploaded on
# 2026-10-14) is the release whose run is measured above. Choosing a newer one would mean pinning a
# version nobody has measured here. It would also not change the entries in osv-scanner.toml, because
# on 2026-10-26 the package index showed every release from 1.180.0 to 1.182.1 requiring the same
# mcp==1.29.0 and opentelemetry-api~=1.37.0.
#
# 680 OF 1081 FILES, AND THAT IS NOT A FAULT. Semgrep's own default ignore patterns exclude
# tests/, which is 393 of this repository's files on main at 845c8a4, and one picture is skipped
# for being over 1 MB. That leaves 688 and the scan read 680, so eight files are neither tests nor
# the oversized picture - the other pictures are what is left, but that is the arithmetic of the
# count and not a line semgrep prints. The same eight were left over on 2026-10-14, when the scan
# read 399 of 407 files outside tests/. The growth since then is 281 files added outside tests/,
# of which 221 are the language pages and strings in site/. So a healthy run of this tree reads
# src/, site/, .github/, packaging/ and the root - about seven hundred files today - and a collapse
# to a handful is the shape of a scan that ran somewhere else. The gate prints the number on every
# run for exactly that reason.
#
# Licence, read on 2026-09-22 from that version's own metadata rather than recalled, and read again
# on 2026-10-26 from 1.181.0's, which says the same. The
# package index reports `license_expression` as LGPL-2.1-or-later, with the older `license`
# field null and no licence classifier - which is the modern shape and worth saying, because a
# reader checking the field that used to hold this would find nothing and could conclude the
# licence was unstated. It analyses the source tree in CI and is never linked into anything this
# project ships, so it creates no distribution obligation - see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md for what
# does.
semgrep==1.181.0
